results.title: A comparison review of transfer learning and self ...
results.content: # Review A comparison review of transfer learning and self-supervised learning: Definitions, applications, advantages and limitations. Applications of Transfer Learning and Self-Supervised Learning. Advantages and Limitations of Transfer Learning and Self-Supervised Learning. Transfer learning leverages knowledge learned from pre-training on a large-scale dataset, such as ImageNet, and applies it to a target task with limited labelled data. On the other hand, self-supervised learning focuses on training models using pretext tasks that do not require manual annotation, allowing them to learn valuable representations from large amounts of unlabelled data. In recent years, transfer and self-supervised learning have found applications in various fields, including medical image processing, video recognition, and natural language processing. For example, transfer learning may face domain mismatch issues between the pre-training and target domains, while self-supervised learning requires careful design of pretext tasks to ensure meaningful representations. By providing a comprehensive review of current pre-training methods, this article offers guidance for selecting the best technique for specific deep learning applications to address the data scarcity issue.

results.title: How many epochs are enough to train your model
results.content: Choosing the optimal number of epochs for training a machine learning model is about finding balance. Too many epochs cause overfitting: the model achieves high accuracy on the training set, but struggles with real-world tasks. During an epoch, the model processes each training example at least once and updates its weights based on the computed gradients. For example, patience = 5 means if validation quality doesn’t improve for five consecutive epochs, training ends the model is resorted to its best-performing checkpoint. Simpler models converge faster and can be trained with fewer epochs, though their ability to learn complex dependencies is limited. In NLP, for example, models are evaluated by the number of processed tokens — large language models are typically trained on trillions of tokens, which may represent only a fraction of a single epoch over the full dataset.Training steps (iterations) offer another precise metric, since they count weight updates directly and are not tied to dataset size.

results.title: Enhanced Fine-Tuning Techniques for Domain-Specific AI ...
results.content: For instance, a language model initially trained on general text data might be fine-tuned with specialized domain data, such as medical journals, to enhance its performance in tasks like disease diagnosis or medical information retrieval. **Transfer Learning**: Leveraging general-purpose models as a starting point, then fine-tuning with domain-specific data, can yield high-performance results with less data. To apply transfer learning, start by loading a pre-trained model, freezing specific layers to retain learned features, and fine-tuning the remaining layers on domain-specific data. In this example, we load a pre-trained model (e.g., InceptionV3 for image classification), freeze initial layers, and fine-tune the remaining layers with domain-specific data. A structured approach to fine-tuning pre-trained models ensures optimized domain-specific performance, capturing nuances unique to fields like healthcare, finance, or legal analysis.”. This approach is particularly useful in transfer learning and fine-tuning scenarios, as it allows a model to retain general knowledge from its pre-trained state while learning new, domain-specific information in the unfrozen layers.
